sanskrit: paśya bhīmaṃ mahābāho rākṣasendravaśaṃ gatam padavīm asya gaccha tvaṃ mā vicāraya pāṇḍava
english: "Look, O mighty-armed one, Bhīma has fallen under the power of the lord of the rākṣasas. Go to his aid, O Pāṇḍava, and do not hesitate."

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca yudhāmanyūttamaujasau sahitā draupadeyāś ca karṇaṃ yāntu mahārathāḥ
english: "Let Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas, together with the sons of Draupadī, those great chariot-warriors, advance upon Karṇa."

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca yuyudhānaś ca vīryavān itarān rākṣasān ghnantu śāsanāt tava pāṇḍava
english: "Let Nakula and Sahadeva, and the valiant Yuyudhāna, slay the other rākṣasas at your command, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: tvam apīmāṃ mahābāho camūṃ droṇapuraskṛtām vārayasva naravyāghra mahad dhi bhayam āgatam
english: "And you yourself, O mighty-armed tiger among men, hold back this host that has Droṇa at its head, for a great peril has come upon us."

sanskrit: evam ukte tu kṛṣṇena yathoddiṣṭā mahārathāḥ jagmur vaikartanaṃ karṇaṃ rākṣasāṃś cetarān raṇe
english: When Kṛṣṇa had spoken thus, the great chariot-warriors, as directed, advanced in battle against Vaikartana Karṇa and against the other rākṣasas.

sanskrit: atha pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭaiḥ śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ dhanuś ciccheda bhīmasya rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān
english: Then with arrows like venomous serpents, loosed from a bow drawn to its full, the mighty lord of the rākṣasas severed the bow of Bhīma.

sanskrit: hayāṃś cāsya śitair bāṇaiḥ sārathiṃ ca mahābalaḥ jaghāna miṣataḥ saṃkhye bhīmasenasya bhārata
english: And with sharp shafts that mighty one slew his horses and his charioteer in battle, O Bhārata, before the very eyes of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: so 'vatīrya rathopasthād dhatāśvo hatasārathiḥ tasmai gurvīṃ gadāṃ ghorāṃ sa vinadyotsasarja ha
english: His horses slain and his charioteer slain, he leapt down from the body of the chariot and, roaring aloud, hurled at him his heavy and terrible mace.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ bhīmanirghoṣām āpatantīṃ mahāgadām gadayā rākṣaso ghoro nijaghāna nanāda ca
english: Then, as that great mace came hurtling on with a fearsome roar, the dread rākṣasa struck it down with his own mace, and let forth a shout.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā rākṣasendrasya ghoraṃ karma bhayāvaham bhīmasenaḥ prahṛṣṭātmā gadām āśu parāmṛśat
english: Beholding that terrible, terror-striking feat of the lord of the rākṣasas, Bhīmasena, his spirit elated, swiftly took up his mace.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ nararakṣasoḥ gadānipātasaṃhrādair bhuvaṃ kampayator bhṛśam
english: A tumultuous combat broke out between the man and the rākṣasa, the crash of their falling maces making the earth tremble violently.

sanskrit: gadāvimuktau tau bhūyaḥ samāsādyetaretaram muṣṭibhir vajrasaṃhrādair anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: Their maces flung away, the two closed once more upon each other and smote one another with fists that crashed like thunderbolts.

sanskrit: rathacakrair yugair akṣair adhiṣṭhānair upaskaraiḥ yathāsannam upādāya nijaghnatur amarṣaṇau
english: Seizing whatever lay at hand—chariot-wheels, yokes, axles, chariot-frames, and gear—the two furious warriors struck each other down.

sanskrit: tau vikṣarantau rudhiraṃ samāsādyetaretaram mattāv iva mahānāgāv akṛṣyetāṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Streaming blood, grappling with one another, they dragged each other back and forth again and again, like two great rutting elephants.

sanskrit: tam apaśyad dhṛṣīkeśaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ hite rataḥ sa bhīmasenarakṣārthaṃ haiḍimbaṃ pratyacodayat
english: Hṛṣīkeśa, devoted to the welfare of the Pāṇḍavas, beheld this; and to protect Bhīmasena he urged on the son of Hiḍimbā.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saṃprekṣya samare bhīmaṃ rakṣasā grastam antikāt vāsudevo 'bravīd vākyaṃ ghaṭotkacam idaṃ tadā
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing Bhīma hard pressed in battle, seized close at hand by the rākṣasa, Vāsudeva then spoke these words to Ghaṭotkaca:

sanskrit: paśya bhīmaṃ mahābāho rakṣasā grastam antikāt paśyatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ tava caiva mahādyute
english: "Look, O mighty-armed one of great splendor, how Bhīma is held fast at close quarters by the rākṣasa, in the sight of all the armies and of you yourself."

sanskrit: sa karṇaṃ tvaṃ samutsṛjya rākṣasendram alāyudham jahi kṣipraṃ mahābāho paścāt karṇaṃ vadhiṣyasi
english: "Leave off Karṇa, and quickly slay Alāyudha, lord of the rākṣasas, O mighty-armed one; Karṇa you shall slay afterward."

sanskrit: sa vārṣṇeyavacaḥ śrutvā karṇam utsṛjya vīryavān yuyudhe rākṣasendreṇa bakabhrātrā ghaṭotkacaḥ tayoḥ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ babhūva niśi rakṣasoḥ
english: Hearing the words of the Vṛṣṇi hero, the valiant Ghaṭotkaca left off Karṇa and fought with the lord of the rākṣasas, the brother of Baka; and a most tumultuous combat arose between those two rākṣasas in the night.

sanskrit: alāyudhasya yodhāṃs tu rākṣasān bhīmadarśanān vegenāpatataḥ śūrān pragṛhītaśarāsanān
english: Now the warriors of Alāyudha, rākṣasas terrible to behold, brave and gripping their bows, were rushing on with speed.

sanskrit: āttāyudhaḥ susaṃkruddho yuyudhāno mahārathaḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca cicchidur niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Weapons in hand and greatly enraged, Yuyudhāna the great chariot-warrior, with Nakula and Sahadeva, cut them down with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: sarvāṃś ca samare rājan kirīṭī kṣatriyarṣabhān paricikṣepa bībhatsuḥ sarvataḥ prakṣipañ śarān
english: And in that battle, O king, the diademed Bībhatsu scattered all those bulls among the kṣatriyas, loosing his arrows on every side.

sanskrit: karṇaś ca samare rājan vyadrāvayata pārthivān dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍyādīn pāñcālānāṃ mahārathān
english: And Karṇa in that battle, O king, drove off the princes—Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Śikhaṇḍin and the rest, the great chariot-warriors of the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: tān vadhyamānān dṛṣṭvā tu bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ abhyayāt tvaritaḥ karṇaṃ viśikhān vikiran raṇe
english: Seeing them being slaughtered, Bhīma of terrible prowess advanced swiftly upon Karṇa, scattering his shafts in the battle.

sanskrit: tatas te 'py āyayur hatvā rākṣasān yatra sūtajaḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ te karṇaṃ yodhayām āsuḥ pāñcālā droṇam eva ca
english: Then, having slain the rākṣasas, Nakula and Sahadeva and Sātyaki the great chariot-warrior came to where the son of the sūta stood; they engaged Karṇa in battle, while the Pāñcālas engaged Droṇa.

sanskrit: alāyudhas tu saṃkruddho ghaṭotkacam ariṃdamam parigheṇātikāyena tāḍayām āsa mūrdhani
english: But Alāyudha, in great fury, struck Ghaṭotkaca, that crusher of foes, upon the head with a huge iron club.

sanskrit: sa tu tena prahāreṇa bhaimasenir mahābalaḥ īṣan mūrchānvito ''tmānaṃ saṃstambhayata vīryavān
english: By that blow the mighty son of Bhīmasena was a little dazed, yet, valorous as he was, he steadied himself.

sanskrit: tato dīptāgnisaṃkāśāṃ śataghaṇṭām alaṃkṛtām cikṣepa samare tasmai gadāṃ kāñcanabhūṣaṇām
english: Then in that combat he hurled at him a mace adorned with gold, bright as blazing fire and decked with a hundred bells.

sanskrit: sā hayān sārathiṃ caiva rathaṃ cāsya mahāsvanā cūrṇayām āsa vegena visṛṣṭā bhīmakarmaṇā
english: Loosed with force by that doer of terrible deeds, the loud-clanging mace ground his horses, his charioteer, and his chariot to powder.

sanskrit: sa bhagnahayacakrākṣo viśīrṇadhvajakūbaraḥ utpapāta rathāt tūrṇaṃ māyām āsthāya rākṣasīm
english: His horses, wheels, and axle broken, his banner and chariot-pole shattered, he sprang up swiftly from the chariot, taking to rākṣasa sorcery.

sanskrit: sa samāsthāya māyāṃ tu vavarṣa rudhiraṃ bahu vidyudvibhrājitaṃ cāsīt timirābhrākulaṃ nabhaḥ
english: Resorting to that illusion, he rained down a great flood of blood, and the sky grew thick with murky clouds, lit by flashes of lightning.

sanskrit: tato vajranipātāś ca sāśanistanayitnavaḥ mahāṃś caṭacaṭāśabdas tatrāsīd dhi mahāhave
english: Then came the fall of thunderbolts with lightning and crashing thunder, and a mighty crackling din arose there in that great battle.

sanskrit: tāṃ prekṣya vihitāṃ māyāṃ rākṣaso rākṣasena tu ūrdhvam utpatya haiḍimbas tāṃ māyāṃ māyayāvadhīt
english: Seeing the illusion wrought by one rākṣasa, the other rākṣasa, the son of Hiḍimbā, sprang upward and undid that illusion by an illusion of his own.

sanskrit: so 'bhivīkṣya hatāṃ māyāṃ māyāvī māyayaiva hi aśmavarṣaṃ sutumulaṃ visasarja ghaṭotkace
english: When the master of illusion saw his illusion destroyed, by illusion he loosed a most violent rain of stones upon Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: aśmavarṣaṃ sa tad ghoraṃ śaravarṣeṇa vīryavān diśo vidhvaṃsayām āsa tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: That terrible rain of stones the valiant one scattered to all quarters with a downpour of arrows, and the deed seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tato nānāpraharaṇair anyonyam abhivarṣatām āyasaiḥ parighaiḥ śūlair gadāmusalamudgaraiḥ
english: Then the two rained down upon each other with weapons of every kind—with iron clubs, spears, maces, pestles, and mallets,

sanskrit: pinākaiḥ karavālaiś ca tomaraprāsakampanaiḥ nārācair niśitair bhallaiḥ śaraiś cakraiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ
english: with trident-staves and swords, with lances, javelins, and pikes, with iron shafts, sharp broad-headed arrows, ordinary arrows, discuses, and battle-axes,

sanskrit: ayoguḍair bhiṇḍipālair gośīrṣolūkhalair api utpāṭya ca mahāśākhair vividhair jagatīruhaiḥ
english: with iron balls, with slings, with ox-headed clubs and mortars, and with all manner of great-branched trees torn up by the roots.

sanskrit: śamīpīlukarīraiś ca śamyākaiś caiva bhārata iṅgudair badarībhiś ca kovidāraiś ca puṣpitaiḥ
english: With śamī, pīlu, and karīra trees, and with śamyāka too, O Bhārata, with iṅgudas and jujubes, and with kovidāras in full flower,

sanskrit: palāśair arimedaiś ca plakṣanyagrodhapippalaiḥ mahadbhiḥ samare tasminn anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: with palāśas and arimedas, with great plakṣas, banyans, and pippal trees, they smote one another in that combat.

sanskrit: vividhaiḥ parvatāgraiś ca nānādhātubhir ācitaiḥ teṣāṃ śabdo mahān āsīd vajrāṇāṃ bhidyatām iva
english: And with mountain-peaks of every sort, studded with manifold minerals, they fought; and the din of these was great, as of thunderbolts splitting asunder.

sanskrit: yuddhaṃ tad abhavad ghoraṃ bhaimyalāyudhayor nṛpa harīndrayor yathā rājan vālisugrīvayoḥ purā
english: Terrible was that combat between the son of Bhīma and Alāyudha, O king, like the strife of old between those lords of the monkeys, Vālin and Sugrīva.

sanskrit: tau yuddhvā vividhair ghorair āyudhair viśikhais tathā pragṛhya niśitau khaḍgāv anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: Having fought with terrible weapons of every kind and with arrows, the two seized their sharp swords and smote at one another.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyam abhidrutya keśeṣu sumahābalau bhujābhyāṃ paryagṛhṇītāṃ mahākāyau mahābalau
english: Rushing each upon the other, those two of vast bodies and mighty strength grasped one another by the hair and gripped each other with their arms.

sanskrit: tau bhinnagātrau prasvedaṃ susruvāte janādhipa rudhiraṃ ca mahākāyāv abhivṛṣṭāv ivācalau
english: Their limbs torn, those two of vast frame streamed with sweat and blood, O ruler of men, like two mountains drenched with rain.

sanskrit: athābhipatya vegena samudbhrāmya ca rākṣasam balenākṣipya haiḍimbaś cakartāsya śiro mahat
english: Then, falling upon him with speed, the son of Hiḍimbā whirled the rākṣasa about, hurled him down with all his might, and struck off his great head.

sanskrit: so 'pahṛtya śiras tasya kuṇḍalābhyāṃ vibhūṣitam tadā sutumulaṃ nādaṃ nanāda sumahābalaḥ
english: And bearing off that head adorned with its two earrings, the mighty one then let forth a most tumultuous roar.

sanskrit: hataṃ dṛṣṭvā mahākāyaṃ bakajñātim ariṃdamam pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva siṃhanādān vinedire
english: Seeing slain that vast-bodied crusher of foes, the kinsman of Baka, the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas raised their lion-roars.

sanskrit: tato bherīsahasrāṇi śaṅkhānām ayutāni ca avādayan pāṇḍaveyās tasmin rakṣasi pātite
english: Then, when that rākṣasa had been laid low, the Pāṇḍavas sounded thousands of kettledrums and tens of thousands of conches.

sanskrit: atīva sā niśā teṣāṃ babhūva vijayāvahā vidyotamānā vibabhau samantād dīpamālinī
english: Most rich in victory did that night become for them, and it shone resplendent all around, garlanded with lamps.

sanskrit: alāyudhasya tu śiro bhaimasenir mahābalaḥ duryodhanasya pramukhe cikṣepa gatacetanam
english: And the mighty son of Bhīmasena flung the lifeless head of Alāyudha down before Duryodhana.

sanskrit: atha duryodhano rājā dṛṣṭvā hatam alāyudham babhūva paramodvignaḥ saha sainyena bhārata
english: Then King Duryodhana, seeing Alāyudha slain, became utterly stricken with dismay, together with his army, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tena hy asya pratijñātaṃ bhīmasenam ahaṃ yudhi hanteti svayam āgamya smaratā vairam uttamam
english: For that one, coming of his own accord and remembering an old and grievous enmity, had promised him: "I will slay Bhīmasena in battle."

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ sa tena hantavya ity amanyata pārthivaḥ jīvitaṃ cirakālāya bhrātṝṇāṃ cāpy amanyata
english: The king had believed that Bhīma would surely be slain by him, and had reckoned upon long life for himself and for his brothers.

sanskrit: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā vinihataṃ bhīmasenātmajena vai pratijñāṃ bhīmasenasya pūrṇām evābhyamanyata
english: But seeing him struck down by the son of Bhīmasena, he reckoned the vow of Bhīmasena as good as fulfilled.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca nihatyālāyudhaṃ rakṣaḥ prahṛṣṭātmā ghaṭotkacaḥ nanāda vividhān nādān vāhinyāḥ pramukhe sthitaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having slain the rākṣasa Alāyudha, Ghaṭotkaca, his spirit elated, standing before the host, let forth roars of every kind.

sanskrit: tasya taṃ tumulaṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā kuñjarakampanam tāvakānāṃ mahārāja bhayam āsīt sudāruṇam
english: Hearing that tumultuous cry of his, which made the elephants tremble, a most dreadful fear came upon your men, O great king.

sanskrit: alāyudhaviṣaktaṃ tu bhaimaseniṃ mahābalam dṛṣṭvā karṇo mahābāhuḥ pāñcālān samupādravat
english: Seeing the mighty son of Bhīmasena entangled with Alāyudha, the mighty-armed Karṇa rushed upon the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: daśabhir daśabhir bāṇair dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍinau dṛḍhaiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair bibheda nataparvabhiḥ
english: With ten arrows each—firm shafts with bent joints, loosed from a fully drawn bow—he pierced Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramanārācair yudhāmanyūttamaujasau sātyakiṃ ca rathodāraṃ kampayām āsa mārgaṇaiḥ
english: Then with excellent iron shafts he set trembling Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas, and the noble chariot-warrior Sātyaki, with his arrows.

sanskrit: teṣām abhyasyatāṃ tatra sarveṣāṃ savyadakṣiṇam maṇḍalāny eva cāpāni vyadṛśyanta janādhipa
english: As all of them plied their bows there, to left and right, their bows appeared as so many circles, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ jyātalanirghoṣo rathanemisvanaś ca ha meghānām iva gharmānte babhūva tumulo niśi
english: The twang of their bowstrings and the rattle of their chariot-rims grew tumultuous in the night, like the roar of clouds at the close of the hot season.

sanskrit: jyānemighoṣastanayitnumān vai; dhanustaḍin maṇḍalaketuśṛṅgaḥ śaraughavarṣākulavṛṣṭimāṃś ca; saṃgrāmameghaḥ sa babhūva rājan
english: With the twang of bowstrings and the rattle of rims for its thunder, with bows for its lightning and circled bow-arcs for its banner-peaks, raining a turbid downpour of arrow-floods—such a battle-cloud did he become, O king.

sanskrit: tad uddhataṃ śaila ivāprakampyo; varṣaṃ mahac chailasamānasāraḥ vidhvaṃsayām āsa raṇe narendra; vaikartanaḥ śatrugaṇāvamardī
english: Unshakable as a mountain, with might equal to a mountain's, Vaikartana the crusher of enemy hosts shattered in battle that uprushing great downpour, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tato 'tulair vajranipātakalpaiḥ; śitaiḥ śaraiḥ kāñcanacitrapuṅkhaiḥ śatrūn vyapohat samare mahātmā; vaikartanaḥ putrahite ratas te
english: Then with peerless, sharp arrows like falling thunderbolts, their shafts bright with gold, the great-souled Vaikartana, intent upon the welfare of your sons, drove off his foes in the battle.

sanskrit: saṃchinnabhinnadhvajinaś ca ke cit; ke cic charair arditabhinnadehāḥ ke cid visūtā vihayāś ca ke cid; vaikartanenāśu kṛtā babhūvuḥ
english: Some had their banners hewn and broken, some had their bodies torn and pierced by his shafts, some were stripped of charioteer, and some of horses—so swiftly were they made by Vaikartana.

sanskrit: avindamānās tv atha śarma saṃkhye; yaudhiṣṭhiraṃ te balam anvapadyan tān prekṣya bhagnān vimukhīkṛtāṃś ca; ghaṭotkaco roṣam atīva cakre
english: Finding no refuge in the battle, they fell back upon the host of Yudhiṣṭhira; and beholding them broken and turned to flight, Ghaṭotkaca was seized with exceeding wrath.

sanskrit: āsthāya taṃ kāñcanaratnacitraṃ; rathottamaṃ siṃha ivonnanāda vaikartanaṃ karṇam upetya cāpi; vivyādha vajrapratimaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ
english: Mounting that splendid chariot bright with gold and gems, he roared aloud like a lion, and drawing near to Vaikartana Karṇa, he pierced him with shafts like thunderbolts.

sanskrit: tau karṇinārācaśilīmukhaiś ca; nālīkadaṇḍaiś ca savatsadantaiḥ varāhakarṇaiḥ saviṣāṇaśṛṅgaiḥ; kṣurapravarṣaiś ca vinedatuḥ kham
english: With barbed darts, iron shafts, and arrows; with tubular and staff-like arrows, and calf-toothed ones; with boar-eared and horn-tipped shafts, and with showers of razor-arrows, the two made the sky resound.

sanskrit: tad bāṇadhārāvṛtam antarikṣaṃ; tiryaggatābhiḥ samare rarāja suvarṇapuṅkhajvalitaprabhābhir; vicitrapuṣpābhir iva srajābhiḥ
english: The mid-air, veiled in showers of arrows flying crosswise through the battle, shone with the blazing radiance of golden-feathered shafts, as though with garlands of many-colored flowers.

sanskrit: samaṃ hi tāv apratimaprabhāvāv; anyonyam ājaghnatur uttamāstraiḥ tayor hi vīrottamayor na kaś cid; dadarśa tasmin samare viśeṣam
english: Evenly matched and of incomparable might, the two struck at one another with their finest weapons; and in that battle no one could mark any difference between those two foremost of heroes.

sanskrit: atīva tac citram atīva rūpaṃ; babhūva yuddhaṃ ravibhīmasūnvoḥ samākulaṃ śastranipātaghoraṃ; divīva rāhvaṃśumatoḥ prataptam
english: Most wondrous and most splendid in form was that battle between the son of the Sun and the son of Bhīma, turbulent and terrible with the fall of weapons, blazing as if in the sky between Rāhu and the radiant Sun.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkaco yadā karṇaṃ na viśeṣayate nṛpa tadā prāduścakārogram astram astravidāṃ varaḥ
english: When Ghaṭotkaca could gain no advantage over Karṇa, O king, then that foremost of those skilled in weapons brought forth a fearsome missile.

sanskrit: tenāstreṇa hayān pūrvaṃ hatvā karṇasya rākṣasaḥ sārathiṃ caiva haiḍimbaḥ kṣipram antaradhīyata
english: With that weapon the rākṣasa, the son of Hiḍimbā, first slew Karṇa's horses and his charioteer, and then swiftly vanished from sight.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tathā hy antarhite tasmin kūṭayodhini rākṣase māmakaiḥ pratipannaṃ yat tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When that rākṣasa, that fighter by guile, had thus vanished, tell me, Saṃjaya, what my men then did.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca antarhitaṃ rākṣasaṃ taṃ viditvā; saṃprākrośan kuravaḥ sarva eva kathaṃ nāyaṃ rākṣasaḥ kūṭayodhī; hanyāt karṇaṃ samare 'dṛśyamānaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Knowing that the rākṣasa had vanished, all the Kurus cried out together: "How shall this rākṣasa, this fighter by guile, unseen, not slay Karṇa in the battle?"

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo laghucitrāstrayodhī; sarvā diśo vyāvṛṇod bāṇajālaiḥ na vai kiṃ cid vyāpatat tatra bhūtaṃ; tamobhūte sāyakair antarikṣe
english: Then Karṇa, fighting with deft and dazzling skill in weapons, covered every quarter with nets of arrows; yet no creature there was struck, in the mid-air made dark with his shafts.

sanskrit: na cādadāno na ca saṃdadhāno; na ceṣudhī spṛśamānaḥ karāgraiḥ adṛśyad vai lāghavāt sūtaputraḥ; sarvaṃ bāṇaiś chādayāno 'ntarikṣam
english: Neither drawing out an arrow, nor fitting it to the string, nor touching his quivers with his fingertips could the son of the sūta be seen, so swift was he—yet he covered the whole sky with arrows.

sanskrit: tato māyāṃ vihitām antarikṣe; ghorāṃ bhīmāṃ dāruṇāṃ rākṣasena saṃpaśyāmo lohitābhraprakāśāṃ; dedīpyantīm agniśikhām ivogrām
english: Then we beheld an illusion wrought in the mid-air by the rākṣasa—horrible, frightful, and dread—glowing red as a blood-hued cloud, blazing fierce like a tongue of fire.

sanskrit: tatas tasyā vidyutaḥ prādurāsann; ulkāś cāpi jvalitāḥ kauravendra ghoṣaś cānyaḥ prādurāsīt sughoraḥ; sahasraśo nadatāṃ dundubhīnām
english: Then out of it lightnings broke forth, and blazing meteors too, O lord of the Kurus; and another sound arose, most terrible, as of thousands of kettledrums thundering.
